risk_register.description: Historical MATE variables differ among years
risk_register.mitigation: Use an explicit year-by-variable matrix; harmonise only defensible common variables; retain year-specific measurements as secondary information. [Affects: WP1 (Data Harmonisation and Physiological Stress Definition)]

risk_register.description: Effective biological sample size is limited
risk_register.mitigation: Use repeated-measure/hierarchical structure, conservative feature reduction and parsimonious modelling; no deep-learning dependency. [Affects: WP2 (HUN-REN Modelling and ELTE Scale Harmonisation)]

risk_register.description: Farmer site lacks modern monitoring infrastructure
risk_register.mitigation: Install project meteorological station and soil sensors before the validation campaign; define maintenance and data-quality responsibilities. [Affects: WP3 (Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation)]

risk_register.description: Primary farmer access changes or is interrupted
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written access; maintain the Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route as a contingency subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability. [Affects: WP3 (Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation)]

risk_register.description: ELTE instrument access or timing is constrained
risk_register.mitigation: Use a written equipment/operation schedule; prioritise key physiological dates; retain physiology/proximal sensing as the core pathway if individual UAV campaigns are missed. [Affects: WP2 (HUN-REN Modelling and ELTE Scale Harmonisation)]

risk_register.description: Field geometry or clouds limit Sentinel-2 interpretation
risk_register.mitigation: Use Sentinel only where valid pixels support field-scale inference; rely on UAV/proximal observations for finer spatial scales. [Affects: WP3 (Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation)]

Treat transfer loss as a scientific result; quantify uncertainty and use limited transparent recalibration rather than hiding the gap. [Affects: WP3 (Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation)]

Develop incrementally from the existing desktop prototype; scientific deliverables remain primary; prioritise validated core functions over feature breadth. [Affects: WP4 (DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation)]

Design placement around usability/interoperability requirements and protected/coded extracts; unrestricted customer-system access is not a project dependency. [Affects: WP5 (AgroVIR Non-Academic Placement)]

Use for approved research; maintain background/foreground inventory and conduct institutional data-rights/IP assessment before commercial exploitation. [Affects: WP4 (DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation)]

ethics_assessment.self_assessment_statement: An ethics self-assessment is completed as an integral part of this proposal, in line with the Tier 1 rule that applicants must complete an ethics self-assessment and that projects with ethics issues may undergo ethics review with ethics requirements becoming contractual obligations (implementation_constraints.json ethics_self_assessment_required; ethics_appraisal_summary). The action focuses exclusively on civil agricultural applications and involves no excluded activities (human-embryo, cloning, or heritable-genome-modification research), consistent with the Tier 1 civil-focus constraint. Two ethics issues are identified and addressed above: (ETH-01) the development and deployment of AI/ML-based agricultural decision-support tools, addressed through interpretability, uncertainty quantification and responsible-recommendation design; and (ETH-02) processing of data extracts during interoperability testing, addressed by using only protected/coded or anonymised extracts and by obtaining written field-access arrangements, with processing to comply with applicable data-protection legislation. On gender: the beneficiary and academic participating organisations are expected to maintain gender equality plans where the Tier 1 eligibility rule applies (gender_equality_plan_eligibility), and the action will promote equal opportunities and, to the extent possible, gender balance at all levels of personnel including supervisory and managerial level (gender_management_balance_guidance). Regarding integration of the gender dimension in research and innovation content: this follows the Tier 1 default rule that it is mandatory unless the topic explicitly states non-relevance. No Tier 2B exemption source is currently cited in this Phase 6 artifact; Phase 8 drafting must either add the relevant Tier 2B topic-source reference or keep the claim framed as pending call-specific confirmation. On open science: the fellowship's training activities integrate transferable and digital skills and foster Open Science, knowledge valorisation and research integrity, and prepare the fellow for digitally enabled collaboration (FAIR data), as evidenced in the Tier 2B scope requirement SR-06 (Scope — Training activities) and call constraint CC-10 (Scope — Training activities); a Data Management Plan is delivered as a distinct deliverable within the first six months. Note on derivative flags: the Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: true and gender_plan_required: true as compliance flags derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path cites an ethics review or a gender equality plan as a topic-specific mandate for this call, so these are treated as Tier 3 derivative compliance flags rather than confirmed call-specific mandates, while the underlying ethics self-assessment and gender requirements are grounded in Tier 1 extracted rules.
